issues.title: [BUG] `--skill` subset selection is ignored for a non-package skill collection repo (all skills get installed)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug** When installing from a skill-collection repository that is **not** an APM package, the `--skill` flag (intended to install only a subset of skills) is silently ignored: instead of the single named skill, **every** skill in the repository gets integrated. Following the docs ["Install only a subset of skills from a bundle"](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/reference/cli/install/#install-only-a-subset-of-skills-from-a-bundle), I ran a subset install against a skill bundle repo that is not an APM package. Rather than a partial install, all skills in the repository were deployed. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. `apm init` 2. `apm install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills --skill "skills/productivity/grill-me"` 3. Observe that all 15 skills from the repo are integrated, not just `grill-me`. **Expected behavior** Only the specified skill should be installed — the same way the following command works correctly and installs just that one skill: ``` apm install https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill "react-best-practices" ``` **Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: macOS 26.5.1 (Tahoe) - Python Version: N/A (installed via standalone binary, curl installer) - APM Version: 0.18.0 (c393f33) - VSCode Version (if relevant): — **Logs** ``` ❯ apm install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills --skill "skills/productivity/grill-me" [*] Validating 1 package... [+] mattpocock/skills [*] Updated apm.yml with 1 new package(s) [>] Installing 1 new package... [>] Resolving mattpocock/skills... [i] Targets: claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini, opencode, windsurf (source: apm.yml) [+] mattpocock/skills @2bf70051 |-- 15 skill(s) integrated -> 3 targets [!] 1 dependency unpinned: mattpocock/skills -- add #tag or #sha to prevent drift [*] Installed 1 APM dependency in 2.2s. ``` Note `15 skill(s) integrated` even though `--skill` requested a single skill.
Screenshot: all 15 skills deployed despite a single --skill
**Additional context** Changing the skill identifier does not help — the following variants all still integrate all 15 skills: - `apm install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills --skill "productivity/grill-me"` - `apm install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills --skill "grill-me"` Pointing the URL deeper into the repo path fails outright with an install error instead: - `apm install https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/skills/productivity --skill "grill-me"` For context, `mattpocock/skills` stores skills nested under `skills///` and is not authored as an APM package, whereas the working reference (`vercel-labs/agent-skills`) exposes skills at the top level. The `--skill` selection appears to be honored for the latter but ignored for the former. Possibly related: #1535, #872

issues.title: [BUG] apm compile --clean never removes a stale CLAUDE.md after instructions move to .claude/rules/
issues.body:
**Is this a bug?** Yes — companion to #1138; the inverse-direction gap that #1138's dedup fix left open.

## Summary

#1138 (PR #1146) made `apm compile --target claude` skip *creating* a `CLAUDE.md` when instructions are already deployed to `.claude/rules/` (the `files_written == 0 and skip_instructions` guard at `agents_compiler.py:785-791`). That works for a clean checkout.

But it only suppresses **creation**. If a `CLAUDE.md` already exists on disk — authored in an earlier APM version, or generated before `.claude/rules/` was populated — APM **never removes it**, on plain `apm compile` *or* `apm compile --clean`. The stale file lingers indefinitely, and because it predates the dedup it still contains the **full instruction content** that now also lives in `.claude/rules/` — exactly the duplicate-context problem #1138 set out to eliminate.

Both targets share a version of this gap, but the Claude path is worse off: the AGENTS.md path at least has orphan-detection infrastructure (`DistributedAgentsCompiler._find_orphaned_agents_files` / `_cleanup_orphaned_files`), even though it doesn't currently catch the analogous redundant-file case (see the sibling AGENTS.md issue). The CLAUDE.md path has **no cleanup logic at all** — `grep` finds no `rglob("CLAUDE.md")`, no orphan check, no `unlink` anywhere in the Claude compile path.

## Environment

- APM version: 0.19.0
- OS: macOS

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/apm-claude-stale/.apm/instructions && cd /tmp/apm-claude-stale
cat > apm.yml <<'EOF'
name: test-claude-stale
version: 1.0.0
targets: [claude]
EOF
cat > .apm/instructions/global.instructions.md <<'EOF'
---
description: A global instruction
---
This is global guidance.
EOF

# 1. Compile BEFORE .claude/rules/ exists -> CLAUDE.md is written (the "upgrade path" starting state)
apm compile --target claude
cat CLAUDE.md          # full instructions present

# 2. Simulate `apm install` populating .claude/rules/, then recompile
mkdir -p .claude/rules
echo "This is global guidance." > .claude/rules/global.md
apm compile --target claude
cat CLAUDE.md          # STILL THERE, still full instructions -> now duplicated with .claude/rules/

# 3. --clean does not help either
apm compile --target claude --clean
test -f CLAUDE.md && echo "CLAUDE.md STILL present after --clean"
```

## Expected behavior

When instruction dedup fires (`.claude/rules/` already holds the instructions), `apm compile --clean` should **remove a pre-existing, APM-generated `CLAUDE.md`** that would now be redundant — gated on the APM-generated marker (`<!-- Generated by APM CLI -->`, `claude_formatter.py:26`) so a hand-authored `CLAUDE.md` is never deleted. Plain `apm compile` should remain non-destructive (it already correctly avoids *creating* a new one).

The sibling AGENTS.md issue asks for the same `--clean` behavior on that path; fixing both gives consistent, predictable cleanup across targets. (Neither path does this today.)

## Actual behavior

- Step 1 writes a full `CLAUDE.md` (expected for that starting state).
- Step 2: dedup fires and logs *"Instructions already in .claude/rules/ — omitting from CLAUDE.md"*, but the existing `CLAUDE.md` is left untouched — now duplicating `.claude/rules/`.
- Step 3: `apm compile --clean` does **not** remove it. There is no CLAUDE.md cleanup path to invoke.

## Root cause

- `_compile_claude_md` (`agents_compiler.py:617-857`) only guards *new* writes (line 785: `if files_written == 0 and skip_instructions:` → log and write nothing). It never inspects or removes an existing on-disk `CLAUDE.md`.
- There is no Claude analog to `DistributedAgentsCompiler._find_orphaned_agents_files` / `_cleanup_orphaned_files` (`distributed_compiler.py:643`, `722`). The `clean_orphaned` / `--clean` flow is wired only into the AGENTS.md distributed compiler, so it never reaches the Claude target. (Note: even that AGENTS.md flow only removes files no longer in the generated set — it does not currently remove regenerated-but-redundant files; that is the subject of the sibling AGENTS.md issue.)

## Suggested fix

In `_compile_claude_md`, when `skip_instructions` is true and a root `CLAUDE.md` already exists:

1. If `config.clean_orphaned` (`--clean`) is set **and** the existing file carries the APM-generated marker (`claude_formatter.py:26`), remove it and log the removal.
2. If the existing file lacks the marker (hand-authored), leave it and emit the same "hand-authored file will not be overwritten" warning the Copilot-root path already uses (`agents_compiler.py:1131-1138`).
3. Plain `apm compile` (no `--clean`): unchanged — suppress creation only, never delete. Optionally surface a hint that a stale `CLAUDE.md` exists and `--clean` would remove it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Failing test: existing **APM-generated** `CLAUDE.md` + populated `.claude/rules/` + `apm compile --clean` → `CLAUDE.md` removed.
- Hand-authored `CLAUDE.md` (no marker) is **never** removed; warning emitted instead.
- Plain `apm compile` still deletes nothing (non-destructive).
- Clean-checkout behavior from #1138 unchanged (no `CLAUDE.md` ever created).
- `--no-dedup` / `--force-instructions` still regenerate a full `CLAUDE.md` and never trigger removal.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `### Fixed` entry referencing this issue and #1138.

## Related

- #1138 — added the Claude-side dedup + skip-on-create guard (PR #1146); this issue closes the stale-pre-existing-file gap that fix left open.
- #1550 — the Copilot/AGENTS.md dedup parity work. The AGENTS.md path has orphan-removal *infrastructure* the Claude path lacks entirely — but it does **not** currently remove the analogous redundant files either; the sibling AGENTS.md issue addresses that. The two issues should be fixed consistently.

issues.title: Clarify what apm-policy.yml governs (docs + positioning)
issues.body:
Part of #1774

## Problem
`apm-policy.yml` exposes allow/deny lists for dependencies and MCP configs. In practice this can read like a general-purpose permission system, so users ask what APM actually governs and whether it overlaps with controls their agent harness already provides. It does not overlap: APM governs installation and integrity (which sources are trusted, which versions install, whether artifacts are verified, what the lockfile records), while the agent harness governs runtime behavior.

## What to do
- Reframe the policy reference page (docs/src/content/docs/reference/policy-schema.md) to lead with APM's purpose in plain terms: it is the install policy for agent primitives - which sources are trusted, which versions install, and what the lockfile records and verifies.
- Add a short "What apm-policy.yml does NOT govern" section: runtime permissions, sandboxing, what a running agent may do, and harness marketplace enablement. Those are owned by the agent harness.
- Document the meaning of `deny` precisely: APM will not install a denied artifact. `deny` is an install-time decision, not a runtime block.
- Add a one-line FAQ entry: "Does my harness's managed configuration replace APM?" Answer: "No. apm-policy.yml controls what gets installed; your harness controls what runs; they do not overlap."

## Scope discipline
Document only behavior that exists in the released CLI at merge time. The audit visibility for a denied artifact that is present from another source lands with the audit work in this epic (#1775); a one-line follow-up will add that sentence here once it ships. Do not describe unbuilt behavior.

## Why
This removes the most common point of confusion and establishes a consistent vocabulary that the rest of the epic builds on. It is the cheapest, highest-leverage clarity win and can ship first.

## Notes
Docs-only; no code change expected. Keep prose pragmatic and short per the repo docs guidelines. ASCII only.

issues.title: fix(ci): spec-conformance Mode B gate fails open on unresolvable merge-base
issues.body:
## Summary

The OpenAPM "Spec conformance gate" (Mode B silent-extension detector) can **fail open** -- it silently passes a PR that adds uncited substantive code under a normative critical path, instead of firing. A governance gate that passes without evaluating is a supply-chain-integrity hole.

## Root cause

Two compounding factors:

1. `.github/workflows/spec-conformance.yml` checks out with `actions/checkout@v4` and **no `fetch-depth: 0`**. The default checkout is shallow, so `origin/main` history may not be present.
2. `tests/spec_conformance/mode_b_detector.sh` tries to deepen on demand (`git fetch --depth=50`, then `--unshallow`), but when it still cannot resolve the merge-base it does:

   ```sh
   if [ -z "${MB:-}" ]; then
     echo "[!] mode_b: cannot resolve merge-base against $BASE; skipping"
     exit 0
   fi
   ```

   `exit 0` means **skip == pass**. Whether the gate actually evaluates a given PR becomes luck of the checkout.

## Evidence

- PR #1794 (declarable integrity keys) got a real evaluation -> Mode B fired (red), correctly: net-new substantive lines under `policy/` + `install/` with no spec citation.
- PR #1793 (surface unmanaged artifacts) initially showed the gate **green** while its log contained `[!] mode_b: cannot resolve merge-base against origin/main; skipping` -- a non-evaluation, not a real pass. On a later head it resolved the base and correctly fired. Same diff class, opposite gate outcome, purely from checkout depth.

## Impact

A future PR that adds uncited enforcement under a critical path can merge clean if its checkout happens to be shallow and the merge-base is unresolvable. The gate is supposed to be the backstop that forces either a spec citation or an explicit `apm-spec-waiver:` trailer; fail-open removes that guarantee non-deterministically.

## Proposed fix

1. Add `fetch-depth: 0` to the checkout step in `spec-conformance.yml` so the merge-base is deterministically resolvable in CI (root-cause fix -- makes the skip branch unreachable in CI).
2. Defense in depth: when running under CI (`GITHUB_ACTIONS`), make the unresolvable-merge-base branch **fail closed** (`exit 1` with a clear diagnostic) instead of `exit 0`. Preserve the local-dev skip (`exit 0`) so `bash tests/spec_conformance/mode_b_detector.sh` on a shallow local clone stays ergonomic.
3. Update `tests/spec_conformance/test_mode_b_detector.py` to lock the new CI-fail-closed invariant.

## Notes

- This is decoupled from #1794/#1793: both are being resolved by authoring spec citations, which clears Mode B via its spec-concurrent short-circuit regardless of this fix. This issue is about closing the gate hole for all future PRs.
- Report-only framing: this is a CI-integrity correctness fix, not a behaviour change to the spec or the CLI.

Part of the install/integrity governance hardening tracked under #1774.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-17
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-17
**APM Version**: 0.20.0 (788a09a)
**Commands Inspected**: 72 (1 top-level entry, 32 commands, 39 subcommands)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High     | 1     |
| Medium   | 5     |
| Low      | 3     |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm targets` Usage Line Claims Subcommands That Do Not Exist

- **Command**: `apm targets --help`
- **Problem**: The usage line reads `apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`, which tells users that subcommands are expected. However, `apm targets --help` lists **no subcommands**, and any attempted invocation with a subcommand-style argument produces a confusing error (`Error: No such command 'X'`). Users exploring the CLI will reasonably try `apm targets list`, `apm targets show`, etc. and receive no guidance.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Usage: apm targets [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
  ...
  Options:
    --json  Output as JSON instead of a table.
    --all   Include the agent-skills meta-target in JSON output (excluded by default).
    --help  Show this message and exit.
  ```
  No `Commands:` section is shown. Running `apm targets foo` produces:
  ```
  Error: No such command 'foo'.
  ```
- **Root cause**: `targets` is implemented as a `@click.group(invoke_without_command=True)` to allow future subcommands (`apm targets add`, etc.) but none are registered yet. The Click group template bleeds into the usage string.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) remove the `COMMAND [ARGS]...` portion by switching to a plain `@click.command` until real subcommands exist, or (b) suppress the misleading `COMMAND [ARGS]...` from the usage string until subcommands are actually added.

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm cache clean` Has Two Confirmation-Skip Flags With Identical Help Text

- **Command**: `apm cache clean --help`
- **Problem**: The command exposes both `-f, --force` and `-y, --yes`, both described as "Skip confirmation prompt". This creates two issues: (1) duplicate functionality with different flag names, and (2) semantic inconsistency -- `--force` in every other APM command means "overwrite locally-authored files on collision" (see `apm install --help`, `apm update --help`, `apm deps update --help`). A user who has learned that `--force` means "overwrite files" will be confused when it means "skip prompt" in `apm cache clean`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    -f, --force  Skip confirmation prompt
    -y, --yes    Skip confirmation prompt
    --help       Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Compare to `apm install --force`:
  ```
    --force  Overwrite locally-authored files on collision and deploy despite critical
             security findings
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove `-f, --force` from `apm cache clean`. Keep only `-y, --yes` (the consistent pattern: `apm deps clean -y`, `apm runtime remove -y`). The `-f` alias predates the `--yes` convention and creates a semantic collision.

#### `apm deps update` Is Deprecated in Docs But Has No Deprecation Notice in CLI Help

- **Command**: `apm deps update --help`
- **Problem**: The reference documentation at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/deps.md` explicitly marks `apm deps update` as deprecated in favor of `apm update`. However, the CLI help text shows no deprecation warning. Users who run `apm deps update` have no in-band signal that they should migrate to `apm update`.
- **Evidence** (`apm deps update --help` -- no deprecation visible):
  ```
  Usage: apm deps update [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...

    Update APM dependencies to latest refs
  ```
  Compare to `apm install --update` which properly surfaces its deprecation:
  ```
    --update  Update dependencies to latest Git references
              (deprecated: prefer 'apm update' for an interactive plan,
               or 'apm update --yes' for CI)
  ```
  And `apm init --plugin` which does the same:
  ```
    --plugin  (deprecated) Use 'apm plugin init' instead.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add a deprecation notice to the `apm deps update` command description, e.g.: `Update APM dependencies to latest refs. (Deprecated: use 'apm update' instead, which adds an interactive plan, --dry-run, and --yes.)`

#### `apm install --help` Contains a Cross-Command Note About `apm compile`

- **Command**: `apm install --help`
- **Problem**: The description of the `--target` option in `apm install --help` includes a note that belongs in `apm compile --help`, not install's help. This cross-contamination confuses users reading install documentation.
- **Evidence** (inside `apm install --help`, within the `--target` description):
  ```
  Note: '--target all' on 'apm compile' is deprecated; use 'apm compile --all' instead.
  ```
  This sentence is about `apm compile` but appears mid-paragraph in `apm install`'s `--target` option help.
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove this sentence from `apm install`'s `--target` help text. The corresponding deprecation notice (about `--target all`) should be added to `apm compile --help`'s `--target` option description, where it is currently absent.

#### `apm mcp install` Options Are Presented as Prose, Not as CLI Options

- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: `apm mcp install --help` shows its supported options as a block of free-form text rather than structured Click options. This is inconsistent with every other command in the CLI, and makes the options impossible to discover via shell tab-completion.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  Compare to `apm mcp search --help`, which uses proper Click options:
  ```
  Options:
    --limit INTEGER  Number of results to show  [default: 10]
    -v, --verbose    Show detailed output
    --help           Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Expose the common flags (`--transport`, `--url`, `--env`, `--header`, `--registry`, `--mcp-version`, `--dev`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--verbose`, `--no-policy`) as first-class Click options on `apm mcp install`, forwarded to the underlying `apm install --mcp` code path. This enables tab-completion and standard `--help` discoverability.

#### `apm config list` Returns an Error With No Redirect to Correct Alternatives

- **Command**: `apm config list`
- **Problem**: Users familiar with `npm config list`, `git config --list`, or `pip config list` will naturally try `apm config list`. The command fails with a generic error and does not suggest the correct alternatives (`apm config` with no subcommand, or `apm config get` with no argument).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config list
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
  Try 'apm config --help' for help.

  Error: No such command 'list'.
  ```
  The correct alternatives: `apm config` (displays a table of all settings) and `apm config get` (lists all user-settable keys with effective values).
- **Suggested Fix**: Add an `apm config list` alias that forwards to `apm config get` (no argument), providing parity with the ecosystem convention and a better first-run experience.

---

### Low Severity

#### `approve` and `deny` Descriptions End With Periods; No Other Command Does

- **Command**: `apm --help` (top-level command listing)
- **Problem**: In the top-level `apm --help` command table, `approve` and `deny` are the only two commands whose one-line descriptions end with a trailing period. All other 30 commands omit the trailing period.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  approve  Approve executable primitives for installed packages.   <- period
  deny     Revoke executable approval for packages.               <- period
  audit    Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters   <- no period
  cache    Manage the local package cache                         <- no period
  compile  Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files   <- no period
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the trailing periods from the `approve` and `deny` command descriptions to match the convention used by every other command.

#### `apm marketplace --help` Uses Unique Section Headers Not Found in Other Command Groups

- **Command**: `apm marketplace --help`
- **Problem**: `apm marketplace` is the only command group that organizes its subcommands using labelled sections ("Consumer commands:" and "Authoring commands:"). All other command groups (`apm deps`, `apm config`, `apm mcp`, `apm runtime`, etc.) use a flat "Commands:" list.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Consumer commands:
    add       Register a marketplace
    list      List registered marketplaces
    ...
  Authoring commands:
    init      Add a 'marketplace:' block to apm.yml
    ...
  ```
  Compare to `apm deps --help`:
  ```
  Commands:
    clean   Remove all APM dependencies
    info    Show detailed package information
    ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either apply the section-header pattern to other command groups with a logical consumer/author split, or flatten `apm marketplace --help` to a standard "Commands:" list. Consistency matters more than which style is chosen.

#### `apm prune` Is Destructive But Has No `--yes` Flag for CI

- **Command**: `apm prune --help`
- **Problem**: `apm prune` removes installed packages not listed in `apm.yml` (a destructive, potentially irreversible action). It supports `--dry-run` but has no `-y, --yes` flag to skip interactive confirmation in CI pipelines. This is inconsistent with `apm deps clean`, which performs a comparable destructive action and provides both `--dry-run` and `-y, --yes`.
- **Evidence** (`apm prune --help`):
  ```
  Options:
    --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
    --help     Show this message and exit.
  ```
  Compare to `apm deps clean --help`:
  ```
  Options:
    --dry-run  Show what would be removed without removing
    -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt
    --help     Show this message and exit.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `-y, --yes` (skip confirmation prompt) to `apm prune` to enable non-interactive CI use, matching the `apm deps clean` pattern.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Error handling**: All tested error cases (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no argument, `apm config set` with missing args) produce clean, actionable error messages with no stack traces.
- **`apm deps` subcommands**: `list`, `tree`, `info`, `why` -- consistent flags, no style drift, help text matches docs.
- **`apm runtime` subcommands**: `setup`, `list`, `status`, `remove` -- consistent flag naming, experimental notice present, docs match CLI.
- **`apm mcp list/search/show`**: Consistent `--limit` and `--verbose` flags across all three.
- **`apm config get/set/unset`**: All three work as documented; error messages are clear.
- **`apm experimental` subcommands**: All four (`enable`, `disable`, `list`, `reset`) have consistent help text.
- **Deprecation notices on `apm init` flags**: `--plugin` and `--marketplace` correctly show `(deprecated)` inline.
- **`apm unpack`**: Correctly marked `[Deprecated]` with migration path in the description.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works on every command and subcommand tested (72 total).
- **`--dry-run` naming**: Consistent kebab-case spelling across all commands that support it (`apm install`, `apm deps clean`, `apm prune`, `apm pack`, `apm compile`, `apm audit`, `apm publish`, `apm unpack`).

issues.title: [BUG] apm pack omits per-plugin version for INTERNAL/private github.com repos (raw.githubusercontent.com 404, no REST fallback)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
`apm pack` does not emit the per-plugin `version` field in the generated Claude `marketplace.json` when the marketplace packages are remote `git-subdir` references to a **GitHub.com repository with INTERNAL (or private) visibility**.

Root cause: the per-plugin `version` is sourced from a best-effort "metadata enrichment" fetch of each resolved package's remote `apm.yml`(`marketplace/builder.py::_fetch_remote_metadata`). For hosts classified as `github.com`, APM fetches it from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/...`. For **INTERNAL/enterprise** repos, `raw.githubusercontent.com` returns **HTTP 404 even with a valid token**, while the GitHubREST `/contents` API serves the file correctly. APM only falls back to the REST API for GHES/GHE-Cloud hosts, never for `github.com`. Because the fetch fails, `version` is silently omitted.

This is **not** a permissions problem: APM resolves and sends a valid token (`source=gh-auth-token`), and the same 404 happens both locally and in CI.

Secondary factor: the root `apm.yml` marketplace entries pin a semver **range** (`version: "^1.0.0"`), which `_is_display_version()` deliberately rejects, so `version` depends *exclusively* on the remote fetch that is failing.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Have a marketplace repo on **github.com** with **INTERNAL** (or private) visibility, whose root `apm.yml` declares `marketplace.packages[]` as remote `git-subdir` entries (`source: <owner>/<repo>` + `subdir:` + `version: "^1.0.0"`), with `versioning.strategy: tag_pattern`.2. Ensure the referenced packages are tagged (`{name}-v{version}`) so resolution succeeds, and that you are authenticated (`gh auth login`/ a valid token).
3. Run command: `apm pack -m claude --marketplace-path claude=build/marketplace.json`
4. Inspect the output: every entry under `.plugins[]` has `name`, `description`, and `source`, but **no `version`** field.
5. Run with `APM_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` and observe, for every entry:
   ```
   DEBUG apm_cli.marketplace.builder Resolved GitHub token for metadata fetch (source=gh-auth-token)
   DEBUG apm_cli.marketplace.builder Could not fetch remote metadata for <name>
       urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 404: Not Found   (builder.py:975)
   ```
6. Confirm the endpoint mismatch directly (replace `<sha>`):
   ```bash
   # raw CDN — fails even WITH a token
   curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" \
     -H "Authorization: token $(gh auth token)" \
     https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/<sha>/<subdir>/apm.yml
   # -> 404

   # REST contents API — works
   gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/<subdir>/apm.yml?ref=<sha> --jq .name
   # -> apm.yml
   ```

**Expected behavior**
`apm pack` should populate the per-plugin `version` for remote entries on INTERNAL/private github.com repositories — e.g. by falling back to the GitHub REST `/contents` API (which works with the token) when `raw.githubusercontent.com` returns 404, instead of silently droppingthe `version` field. Metadata enrichment should not depend on a CDN that does not serve INTERNAL-visibility repos.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows (MINGW64_NT-10.0)
 - Python Version: 3.12.10
 - APM Version: 0.20.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A

**Logs**
```
DEBUG apm_cli.marketplace.builder Resolved GitHub token for metadata fetch (source=gh-auth-token)
DEBUG apm_cli.marketplace.builder Could not fetch remote metadata for foundations-core
  File ".../apm_cli/marketplace/builder.py", line 975, in _fetch_remote_metadata
urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 404: Not Found
```
(identical 404 for all 12 marketplace entries)

Reproduced endpoint behavior:
- `raw.githubusercontent.com/.../apm.yml` (with `Authorization: token`): HTTP 404
- `gh api repos/.../contents/.../apm.yml?ref=<sha>`: returns the file (200)

**Additional context**
- Relevant code: `marketplace/builder.py::_fetch_remote_metadata` (host branch: `github.com` → raw CDN; else → REST API) and `marketplace/output_mappers.py` (`_is_display_version` rejects semver ranges, so `version` relies solely on the remote-metadata fetch).
- Affects both local runs and CI; independent of token/permissions.
- Workaround on the consumer side: post-process the generated `marketplace.json` to inject each entry's `version` read from the local leaf`apm.yml` (the single source of truth), avoiding the remote fetch entirely.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Standalone `apm mcp export --runtime <target>` command
issues.body:
## Summary

Split out from #20 as a focused residual. Today APM generates runtime MCP config (`.vscode/mcp.json`, `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`, Codex TOML, Claude, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode, IntelliJ) **only as a side effect of `apm install`**. There is no way to (re)generate runtime config on demand without running a full install.

The MCP subcommand surface at HEAD is `install | search | show | list` only -- no `export` (verified: `grep` for `export` across `src/apm_cli/commands/mcp.py` and `src/apm_cli/install/mcp/` returns nothing).

## Ask

A standalone command, e.g.:

```
apm mcp export --runtime vscode
apm mcp export --runtime copilot --runtime codex
```

that materializes runtime config from the already-resolved `apm.yml` + lockfile, without re-resolving/installing dependencies.

## Why

- @TechWatching and enterprise evaluators (#20 thread) want to regenerate per-runtime config deterministically (CI, onboarding, drift repair) decoupled from the install lifecycle.
- The underlying per-runtime writers already exist (adapter layer). This is largely surfacing existing generation as a first-class command.

## Design notes (light)

- Output target precedence and interaction with the lockfile need to be defined (export should read resolved state, not trigger resolution).
- Reuse the existing adapter writers; do not fork config-generation logic.
- Respect the existing `targets:` whitelist semantics (see PR #1336).

## Context

Parent: #20. The bulk of #20's extended-config ask shipped in v0.8.0; this is one of two genuine residuals.

issues.title: [FEATURE] override a consumed primitive's frontmatter (e.g. agent name/description) from apm.yml
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When consuming individual primitives from another repo (e.g. `github/awesome-copilot`
agents) via `dependencies.apm`, the content is materialized verbatim and the
`apm.lock.yaml` integrity check (correctly) forbids editing it. But upstream display
names are often inconsistent or carry vendor taglines — e.g.
`Prompt Builder - Brought to you by microsoft/edge-ai`, or terse slugs like
`sast-sca-security-analyzer`. I would like to normalize these artifacts
without forking or vendoring each file — which loses `apm update` and the
supply-chain gate.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Allow per-dependency frontmatter overrides in `apm.yml`, applied at deploy time and
recorded in `apm.lock.yaml` so they are reproducible and visible in diffs:

```yaml
dependencies:
  apm:
    - repo: github/awesome-copilot
      path: agents/sast-sca-security-analyzer.agent.md
      ref: <sha>
      overrides:
        name: "SAST/SCA Security Analyzer"
        # description: "Reviews dependencies and code for SAST/SCA findings."
```

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-06-25
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-06-25
**APM Version**: 0.21.0 (d9fe3dd)
**Commands Inspected**: 27 (top-level + all subcommands under `deps`, `mcp`, `config`, `runtime`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 4 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm doctor` has no CLI reference documentation page

- **Command**: `apm doctor`
- **Problem**: Every other command in the CLI has a dedicated reference page under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/`. The `apm doctor` command exists and works, and is mentioned in guides, but has no reference page at `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md`.
- **Evidence**:
  - `ls docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` -- no `doctor.md` exists
  - `apm doctor --help` returns valid output:
    ```
    Usage: apm doctor [OPTIONS]

      Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI,
      marketplace config). Reports a pass/fail table and exits non-zero
      if a critical check fails.

    Options:
      -v, --verbose  Show detailed output
      --help         Show this message and exit.
    ```
  - Contrast: `approve.md` covers both `apm approve` AND `apm deny`; `doctor` has no coverage at all in the reference section.
- **Suggested Fix**: Add `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/doctor.md` covering synopsis, all options, exit codes, and examples. The guides content at `docs/src/content/docs/guides/operating-installed-context.md` provides a good starting point.

---

### Medium Severity

#### RST double-backtick notation rendered raw in terminal help text

- **Commands**: `apm approve`, `apm deny`
- **Problem**: The help text for both commands uses RST/Sphinx-style double-backtick markup (` ``text`` `) which renders as literal double-backtick characters in the terminal instead of formatted code. All other commands use plain text or single backticks consistently.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm approve --help
    Adds entries to ``~/.apm/approvals.yml`` (user-local, never committed to
    source control) so that hooks, MCP servers, canvas extensions, and bin/
    executables from the specified packages are deployed during ``apm install``.

  $ apm deny --help
    Removes entries from ``~/.apm/approvals.yml`` (user-local approvals store).
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Replace ` ``~/.apm/approvals.yml`` ` with single backticks in the `approve` and `deny` command docstrings in the source (likely `src/apm_cli/commands/approve.py`).

---

#### `apm config get` shows a misleading "bug in command routing" error for invalid key input

- **Command**: `apm config get`
- **Problem**: Running `apm config get` with an unknown key shows an error message that incorrectly implies a software bug. The user simply entered an invalid key -- it is not a bug.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config get nonexistent_key
  [x] Unknown configuration key: 'nonexistent_key'
  [i] Valid keys: auto-integrate, target, mcp-registry-url, temp-dir, allow-protocol-fallback, prefer-ssh
  [i] This error may indicate a bug in command routing. Please report this issue.
  ```
  The third line is incorrect -- this is normal user input validation, not an internal routing failure.
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the "This error may indicate a bug in command routing" line from this error path, or replace it with: `[i] Run 'apm config get' with no argument to see all effective values.`

---

#### `apm mcp install --help` uses non-standard option presentation

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: Instead of defining options as standard Click options (shown in the `Options:` section), `apm mcp install` embeds option names as an unformatted paragraph inside the help text. This is visually inconsistent with all other commands.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm mcp install --help
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see `apm install --help` for full list): --transport
    [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http] --url URL           Server URL for remote
    transports --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable) --header
    KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable) --registry URL      Custom registry URL
    --mcp-version VER    Pin registry entry to a specific version --dev / --dry-
    run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  All forwarded options are crammed into a single paragraph with no line breaks between option entries.
- **Suggested Fix**: Move the common options list out of the option block and into the epilog/description as a clean formatted list. For example: `All options from 'apm install --mcp NAME' are accepted. Run 'apm install --help' for the full list.`

---

#### `--yes` / `-y` flag has three different descriptions across commands

- **Commands**: `apm deps clean`, `apm update`, `apm runtime remove`
- **Problem**: Three commands share a `-y, --yes` flag for skipping confirmation prompts, but each describes it differently:
  - `apm deps clean`: `Skip confirmation prompt`
  - `apm update`: `Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)`
  - `apm runtime remove`: `Confirm the action without prompting`
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm deps clean --help
    -y, --yes  Skip confirmation prompt

  $ apm update --help
    -y, --yes  Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)

  $ apm runtime remove --help
    -y, --yes  Confirm the action without prompting
  ```
  The third form ("Confirm the action without prompting") is semantically different from "Skip confirmation prompt" and could confuse users.
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize all three to: `Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)`. Update `deps clean` and `runtime remove` source to match `apm update`.

---

### Low Severity

#### Inconsistent trailing punctuation in one-line command descriptions

- **Commands**: `apm pack`, `apm publish`
- **Problem**: Most commands in `apm --help` have no trailing period on their one-line description, but `pack` and `publish` do.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm --help
    compile   Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files   <- no period
    config    Configure APM CLI                                       <- no period
    pack      Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.    <- has period
    publish   Publish a package to a registry.                       <- has period
    run       Run a script with parameters (experimental)            <- no period
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the trailing periods from `pack` and `publish` one-line descriptions to match the majority convention.

---

#### Several command descriptions are truncated in `apm --help`

- **Command**: `apm --help` (main help)
- **Problem**: Five commands have one-line summaries that are too long and are cut off with `...` in the main help view.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm --help
    doctor     Run environment diagnostics (git, network, auth, gh CLI,...
    find       Trace a materialized file back to its contributing...
    install    Install APM and MCP dependencies (supports APM packages,...
    lock       Resolve dependencies and write apm.lock.yaml without...
    uninstall  Remove APM packages, their integrated files, and apm.yml...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Shorten these one-line summaries to fit within a standard 80-character terminal. For example:
  - `doctor`: "Run environment diagnostics"
  - `install`: "Install APM packages and MCP servers"
  - `lock`: "Write apm.lock.yaml without deploying files"

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks:

- `apm init`, `apm compile`, `apm update`, `apm uninstall`, `apm run` -- consistent help structure, correct flag descriptions, no typos
- `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, `apm deps info`, `apm deps clean`, `apm deps update` -- all subcommands present and functional
- `apm mcp search`, `apm mcp show`, `apm mcp list` -- correct `--limit` defaults (20 for list, 10 for search), consistent `-v/--verbose` flag
- `apm config get`, `apm config set`, `apm config unset` -- consistent with documentation (no `list` subcommand in docs or CLI -- both are aligned)
- `apm runtime setup`, `apm runtime list`, `apm runtime status`, `apm runtime remove` -- all present with consistent flag descriptions
- Error handling: All commands produce clean error messages for invalid flags and missing required arguments -- no stack traces observed
- Documentation cross-reference: All CLI commands have corresponding docs coverage (`deny` is correctly combined with `approve` in `approve.md`)
- Flag consistency: `--dry-run` present across all relevant commands; `--verbose`/`-v` consistent where expected; `-g`/`--global` consistent across scoped commands

issues.title: [BUG] apm audit reports false "unintegrated" drift on .agents/skills/ for deps narrowed via per-dependency targets:
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a `dependencies.apm` entry uses per-dependency `targets:` to narrow a skill dependency to a subset of harnesses (e.g. `targets: [claude]`), `apm install` correctly deploys the skill only to that harness's directory (`.claude/skills/`) and **not** to the cross-tool `.agents/skills/` mirror. But `apm audit --ci` still expects `.agents/skills/<dep>/...` and reports those files as `unintegrated` drift, failing the audit even though `apm install` reports the state as up to date.

`apm install` and `apm audit` disagree on the expected file set. This appears to be a gap in the per-dependency `targets:` feature (#1902, v0.22.0): the audit drift replay does not honor per-dependency `targets:`. The `content-integrity` check itself passes — only the `drift` check is wrong.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. `apm.yml` with global `targets: [claude, copilot]` and a skill dependency in object form narrowed to Claude:
   ```yaml
   targets: [claude, copilot]
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - git: owner/repo
         path: skills/some-skill
         targets: [claude]
   ```
2. Run `apm install` → skill lands in `.claude/skills/some-skill`, nothing in `.agents/skills/`. Re-running `apm install` reports `No changes -- install state already up to date`.
3. Run `apm audit --ci` → `Drift detected: N file(s)` with `unintegrated: .agents/skills/some-skill/...`; audit exits non-zero.

**Expected behavior**

`apm audit` should honor per-dependency `targets:` when computing the expected deployed-file set, so a dependency narrowed away from the cross-tool / Copilot targets does not produce false `unintegrated` drift for `.agents/skills/`. Audit should agree with `apm install`.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 11 (also reproduced in CI on Linux / `ubuntu-latest`)
 - Python Version: 3.14.6
 - APM Version: 0.22.0
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): n/a (Claude Code + Copilot targets)

**Logs**

```
[+] Replayed N package(s)
[>] Diffing scratch vs working tree...
[!] Drift detected: <count> file(s)
...
  drift details:
    - unintegrated: .agents/skills/<skill-a>/SKILL.md
    - unintegrated: .agents/skills/<skill-a>/references/<file>.md
    - unintegrated: .agents/skills/<skill-b>/SKILL.md
    ...
[x] 1 of 9 check(s) failed
```

(`content-integrity` check passes; only the `drift` check fails.)

**Additional context**

Related but distinct from closed issues #1716 (`.agents/skills/` content *escaping* the drift check) and #1411 (false *orphaned* drift for non-skill primitives with `auto_create=False`). Here it is false **`unintegrated`** drift specifically triggered by per-dependency `targets:` narrowing. Use case: routing skills to Claude only while keeping Copilot for instructions + MCP servers.

issues.title: [BUG] Anonymous HTTPS clone URLs drop the .git suffix, breaking hosts that require it (e.g. GitBucket)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm install` fails for every dependency hosted on a git server whose
smart-HTTP endpoint is only served at the `.git` path and does not redirect
the bare path — GitBucket is the concrete case. The failure is independent of
ref type (tag / branch / none) and of full vs. shallow clone.

The root cause is an asymmetry in URL construction. APM strips the `.git`
suffix when parsing the dependency URL (`models/dependency/reference.py`),
which is fine as an internal canonical form — but when the clone URL is
rebuilt, only the **anonymous HTTPS** branch fails to re-append it
(`src/apm_cli/utils/github_host.py`, `build_https_clone_url`):

| Builder | Emits `.git`? |
|---|---|
| HTTPS with token (`build_https_clone_url`, token branch) | yes |
| **HTTPS anonymous (`build_https_clone_url`, no-token branch)** | **no** |
| Plain HTTP (`build_clone_http_url`) | yes |
| SSH (`build_ssh_url`, both SCP and `ssh://` forms) | yes |
| GitLab token form (`build_gitlab_https_clone_url`) | yes |

Because `GenericGitBackend` never embeds tokens in URLs (auth is delegated to
git credential helpers, `deps/host_backends.py`), a generic-host dependency
**always** takes the anonymous branch — so for hosts like GitBucket there is
no working HTTPS configuration at all. Writing the `.git` suffix explicitly
in `apm.yml` does not help, because the parser strips it before the builder
runs.

GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket / Gitea all accept the suffix-less form (redirect
or dual-serve), which is presumably why this has gone unnoticed.

**To Reproduce**

With any GitBucket instance (auth via git credential helper):

1. Declare a GitBucket dependency:

   ```yaml
   # apm.yml
   name: gitbucket-repro
   version: 0.0.1
   targets:
     - claude
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - git: https://gitbucket.example.com/git/owner/some-package.git
         ref: v0.1.0
     mcp: []
   ```

2. Run `apm install`.
3. See error (exit code 128 from git; note the missing `.git` in the cmdline).

Sanity check outside APM (same machine, same credentials):

```
$ git ls-remote https://gitbucket.example.com/git/owner/some-package.git   # works
$ git ls-remote https://gitbucket.example.com/git/owner/some-package       # fails
```

**Expected behavior**

The clone URL preserves (or re-appends) the `.git` suffix, matching what the
token, SSH, and plain-HTTP builders already do. The dependency installs over
plain HTTPS with credential-helper auth.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Windows 11
- Python Version: 3.13
- APM Version: 0.23.1 (also reproduced reading `main`)
- Host: GitBucket 4.x behind HTTPS, auth via Git Credential Manager

**Logs**

```
[>] Resolving git/owner/some-package...
[DEBUG] _clone_with_fallback: repo=git/owner/some-package, is_ado=False, is_generic=True, has_token=False, auth_scheme=basic, protocol_pref=none, allow_fallback=False
[DEBUG] transport plan: strict=True, attempts=[('https', False, 'plain HTTPS')]
[DEBUG] Attempting clone with plain HTTPS (URL sanitized)
[x] 1 package failed:
  +- git/owner/some-package -- Failed to download dependency: Failed to clone repository
     ... Last error: Cmd('git') failed due to: exit code(128)
     cmdline: git clone -v --depth=1 --branch=v0.1.0 -- https://gitbucket.example.com/git/owner/some-package
```

**Additional context**

Two aggravating factors make this hard to diagnose in the field:

- GitBucket answers **401 before 404** on the suffix-less path, so git treats
  the repo as private and invokes the credential helper — users get an auth
  dialog (Git Credential Manager) for a URL that can never work, and APM's
  error text ("configure SSH keys or a git credential helper") points at
  authentication rather than the URL.
- The `insteadOf` workaround needs one entry per package repository on every
  developer machine, because a prefix rewrite is the only way to re-append a
  suffix.

Proposed fix — one line in `build_https_clone_url` (plus four test
expectations: three in `tests/unit/test_generic_git_urls.py`, one in
`tests/test_github_downloader_token_precedence.py`):

```diff
     if token:
         # Use x-access-token format which is compatible with GitHub Enterprise and GH Actions
         return f"https://x-access-token:{token}@{netloc}/{repo_ref}.git"
-    return f"https://{netloc}/{repo_ref}"
+    return f"https://{netloc}/{repo_ref}.git"
```

All supported hosts accept the `.git`-suffixed form, so this is
backward-compatible. Verified against a real GitBucket instance: stock 0.23.1
fails as above, and with this patch the same manifest installs successfully
(plain HTTPS, credential-helper auth, no `insteadOf` rewrites). Happy to open
a PR.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report — 2026-07-03
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-07-03
**APM Version**: 0.23.1 (bf4a2b8)
**Commands Inspected**: 30 (`apm` top-level + `init`, `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `run`, `deps` group x7, `mcp` group x5, `config` group x3, `runtime` group x5, plus `lock`, `lock export`, `audit`)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 3 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### High Severity

#### `apm audit` help description is incomplete and uses incorrect terminology

- **Command**: `apm audit`
- **Problem**: The `--help` description ("Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters") is misleading on two counts: (1) it says "packages" but APM's own terminology is "primitives"; (2) it omits the two other major modes the command provides — drift detection and CI gate lockfile/policy checks. A user reading only `apm audit --help` would have no idea the command can run a CI gate (`--ci`), detect drift, or enforce policy.
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI `apm audit --help` first line: `Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters`
  - Source: `src/apm_cli/commands/audit.py:1039` — `@click.command(help="Scan installed packages for hidden Unicode characters")`
  - Docs (`docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/audit.md`) description: `Scan installed primitives for hidden Unicode, drift, and lockfile/policy violations.`
  - Docs description of modes: "`apm audit` is the explicit security and integrity tool. It runs in two modes: **Content scan mode** (default) ... **CI gate mode** (`--ci`). Runs lockfile consistency checks plus drift ..."
  - README: `` `apm audit` rebuilds your agent context in scratch and diffs it against your working tree to catch hand-edits before they ship ``
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `help=` string in `src/apm_cli/commands/audit.py` line 1039 to match the docs: `"Scan installed primitives for hidden Unicode, drift, and policy violations"` (or a similarly complete description).

---

### Medium Severity

#### `apm mcp install --help` uses a non-standard help format

- **Command**: `apm mcp install`
- **Problem**: The help output for `apm mcp install` shows "Common options" as raw plain text embedded inside the Options section, rather than as properly registered Click options. This is unlike every other command in the CLI, making it harder for users to understand which flags are actually accepted vs. just referenced.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Options:
    --help  Show this message and exit.

    Common options (see 'apm install --help' for full list):
      --transport [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http]
      --url URL           Server URL for remote transports
      --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable)
      --header KEY=VALUE  HTTP header (repeatable)
      --registry URL      Custom registry URL
      --mcp-version VER   Pin registry entry to a specific version
      --dev / --dry-run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
  Compare with `apm mcp search --help` or any other subcommand, where all options are uniformly formatted as Click options.
- **Suggested Fix**: Either (a) register the forwarded flags as proper Click options in `apm mcp install` so they appear as standard help entries, or (b) move the "Common options" note to the command description/epilog section so it doesn't appear as a broken options sub-list.

#### `apm config` breaks the command-group "list" pattern

- **Command**: `apm config`
- **Problem**: Every other multi-subcommand group in the CLI provides an explicit `list` subcommand (`apm deps list`, `apm mcp list`, `apm runtime list`). `apm config` instead uses the bare `apm config` (no subcommand) to display all configuration. This inconsistency breaks the predictable pattern users learn from peer commands, and running `apm config list` returns an error (`No such command 'list'`).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config list
  Usage: apm config [OPTIONS] [COMMAND] [ARGS]...
  Try 'apm config --help' for help.

  Error: No such command 'list'.
  ```
  ```
  $ apm deps --help | grep Commands -A5
  Commands:
    clean   ...
    info    ...
    list    List installed APM dependencies
    tree    ...
  $ apm mcp --help | grep Commands -A5
  Commands:
    install  ...
    list     List all available MCP servers
    ...
  $ apm runtime --help | grep Commands -A5
  Commands:
    list    List available and installed runtimes
    ...
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Add an `apm config list` alias that calls the same display logic as `apm config` (no subcommand), making the pattern consistent with `apm deps list`, `apm mcp list`, and `apm runtime list`.

#### `--dry-run` flag description is inconsistent across commands

- **Commands**: `apm install`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm prune`, `apm publish`, `apm audit`
- **Problem**: The `--dry-run` flag uses two different description styles: "Show what would be X without Y" (majority pattern) vs. "Preview without Z." (with trailing period, used only by `apm publish`). `apm update` and `apm compile` also deviate with "Render the update plan and exit without changing anything" and "Preview compilation without writing files" respectively — mixing description styles and capitalization conventions.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm install  --dry-run`: `Show what would be installed without installing`
  - `apm prune    --dry-run`: `Show what would be removed without removing`
  - `apm publish  --dry-run`: `Preview without uploading.`  (period; different verb)
  - `apm update   --dry-run`: `Render the update plan and exit without changing anything`
  - `apm compile  --dry-run`: `Preview compilation without writing files`
  - `apm audit    --dry-run`: `Preview what --strip would remove without modifying files`
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize all `--dry-run` descriptions to the pattern `"Show what would be <verb> without <doing it>"`, e.g.: `"Preview without uploading"` → `"Show what would be published without uploading"`.

---

### Low Severity

#### Trailing period inconsistency in top-level command descriptions

- **Command**: `apm --help` Commands section
- **Problem**: 6 out of 33 top-level commands end their one-line description with a period while the remaining 27 do not. This is inconsistent punctuation within the same help page.
- **Evidence** (commands WITH trailing period):
  - `lifecycle   Inspect, test, and scaffold lifecycle scripts.`
  - `pack        Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.`
  - `publish     Publish a package to a registry.`
  - `self-update Update the APM CLI binary itself to the latest version.`
  - `targets     Show resolved targets for the current project.`
  - `unpack      [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.`
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove the trailing periods from the 6 affected command `help=` strings to match the no-period convention used by the majority.

#### `--verbose` flag descriptions are inconsistently worded across commands

- **Commands**: All commands with `--verbose`
- **Problem**: The `--verbose` flag carries slightly different descriptions across commands, ranging from the generic "Show detailed output" to highly specific "Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics". While some variance is acceptable (verbose mode differs per command), the inconsistency between `apm run --verbose` ("Show detailed output") and `apm update --verbose` ("Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics") makes it hard to predict what verbose mode adds.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm init     --verbose`: `Show detailed output`
  - `apm install  --verbose`: `Show detailed installation information`
  - `apm uninstall--verbose`: `Show detailed removal information`
  - `apm update   --verbose`: `Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics`
  - `apm compile  --verbose`: `Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis`
  - `apm run      --verbose`: `Show detailed output`
  - `apm mcp *    --verbose`: `Show detailed output`
- **Suggested Fix**: Use command-specific descriptions (not generic "Show detailed output") consistently, so users know what extra information each verbose mode provides. For commands where verbose adds no unique detail, "Show detailed output" is acceptable but should be verified.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Error handling**: All tested invalid inputs (`--nonexistent-flag`, missing required args) produce clean usage errors — no stack traces.
- **`--help` / `-h`**: Works correctly on every inspected command and subcommand.
- **`apm init`, `apm install`, `apm uninstall`, `apm update`, `apm compile`, `apm run`**: Core command help text is comprehensive and accurate.
- **`apm deps list/tree/info/clean/why`**: Consistent with documentation and expected behavior.
- **`apm mcp list/search/show`**: Descriptions and defaults match documentation (list default: 20, search default: 10).
- **`apm config get/set/unset`**: Documented and consistent.
- **`apm runtime setup/list/status/remove`**: All subcommands match documentation including `-y/--yes` on `remove`.
- **README command references**: All commands mentioned in README (`apm install`, `apm compile -t`, `apm install --skill`, `apm lock export --format cyclonedx|spdx`, `apm audit --ci`) exist in the CLI and accept the documented flags.
- **Deprecation markers**: `apm deps update` and `apm unpack` are clearly marked as deprecated in both help text and documentation.
- **Exit codes**: Invalid flag = exit 2, missing required arg = exit 2. Consistent with Click conventions.

issues.title: Add additive corporate-CA support: APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE (npm NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS parity)
issues.body:
## Context

Fast-follow from the #2005 / #2004 OS-trust-store work. A red-team review (enterprise-proxy + package-manager-precedent panels) flagged that APM has **no additive CA path**: `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` / `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` **replace** the trust set (and skip truststore injection entirely). Many enterprises hand developers a single corporate-root PEM but do **not** permit OS trust-store edits, so they need "OS roots **plus** this one extra CA", not "only this CA".

This is the standard npm model (`NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, additive) and Node's `--use-system-ca` (system + bundled + extra). APM lacks the equivalent.

## Proposal

Add an additive `APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE` (and optionally `APM_EXTRA_CA_DIR`) that is layered **on top of** the OS trust store rather than replacing it:

- Implement via a scoped `SSLContext` that first loads the OS/certifi defaults, then `load_verify_locations(APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE)` — OS/certifi defaults remain intact.
- Propagate to `apm run` child runtimes through the same `build_child_tls_env()` seam introduced in #2005 (export the extra bundle so Python and Node children both honor it, e.g. `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` for Node runtimes).
- Precedence must be documented explicitly alongside the existing `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` (replace) and `APM_DISABLE_TRUSTSTORE` (opt-out) knobs.

## Acceptance

- An enterprise PEM set via `APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE` is trusted **in addition to** the OS store for both `apm install` and `apm run`.
- e2e test: private-CA server trusted via `APM_EXTRA_CA_BUNDLE` while public HTTPS (OS/certifi roots) still verifies.

Deferred deliberately from #2005 to avoid half-shipping (Node-only) the additive path.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Compile "prompts" primitive to Codex's native ~/.codex/prompts/ format (mirroring how "agents" already targets .codex/agents/*.toml)
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

The `prompts` primitive (`.apm/prompts/*.prompt.md`) compiles to Claude (`.claude/commands/<name>.md`), Copilot (`.github/prompts/<name>.prompt.md`), Cursor (`.cursor/commands/<name>.md`), Gemini (`.gemini/commands/<name>.toml`), and Windsurf (`.windsurf/workflows/<name>.md`) — but explicitly emits nothing for Codex. The docs confirm this is intentional today: "Codex receives nothing. Do not assume a prompt is universal," with the suggested workaround being to ship the functionality as a skill instead.

This is inconsistent with the `agents` primitive (`.apm/agents/*.agent.md`), which does compile to Codex correctly today: `.codex/agents/<name>.toml`, with the markdown body mapped to the `developer_instructions` field (per the "What compiles where" table in the instructions-and-agents docs). So apm already has precedent for faithfully materializing a primitive into a Codex-native format — it just hasn't been done for `prompts` yet.

Note this is a different ask from #1781, which was declined. #1781 proposed generating a *skill* from each prompt entry on Codex — i.e., translating one primitive type into another, which the maintainer correctly identified as a semantic-translation shim outside apm's install-and-integrity scope ("materializing the primitive faithfully is ours" vs. translating between primitive types). This issue instead asks apm to materialize the *same* `prompt` primitive onto Codex's own native prompts mechanism, not convert it into a different primitive — the same category of work already being done for `agents` -> `.codex/agents/*.toml`.

Concretely, Codex CLI already has its own native custom-prompts mechanism: files under `~/.codex/prompts/*.md`, where the filename becomes the invocable command name (e.g. `/prompt-name`). So Codex can support project-authored custom commands in principle — it's specifically apm's prompts compiler that doesn't target it yet.

Without this, any apm package that ships a `prompt` is unusable as a slash-command on Codex, and a developer who wants that command available in Codex has to hand-author and hand-maintain a separate file under `~/.codex/prompts/` outside of apm's install/lock/verify lifecycle, per machine, instead of getting it compiled and kept in sync automatically the way Claude/Copilot/Cursor/Gemini/Windsurf users already do.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Extend the prompts compiler to also emit to Codex's native prompts format when Codex is a target, mirroring the existing agents -> `.codex/agents/<name>.toml` mapping:

- Output: `<name>.md` (body content, since Codex's native prompt files are plain markdown, not TOML)
- Location: Codex's native prompts directory (`~/.codex/prompts/`)

One open question worth surfacing: Codex's native prompts directory is user-global (`~/.codex/prompts/`), unlike apm's other prompt targets which are all project-local (`.claude/commands/`, `.cursor/commands/`, etc.). If apm's install model assumes all materialized output lives inside the project tree, targeting a user-global path may need either (a) a documented exception for this target, or (b) treating it as out of scope for `apm install` and only relevant to `apm install -g`. Flagging this rather than assuming it's a simple addition.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Keep the current behavior (Codex gets nothing for prompts, author ships a skill instead). Works, but means prompt-based packages are simply unreachable as slash-commands on Codex, and there's no compiled/shared path — every developer maintains their own `~/.codex/prompts/` file by hand.
- Generate a skill from prompt entries on Codex (#1781) — already proposed and declined as an out-of-scope semantic translation between primitive types.

**Additional context**

This was noticed while comparing how the `agents` and `prompts` primitives each target Codex — `agents` has full, correct Codex support today (verified empirically via `apm install`), while `prompts` has none, despite Codex having its own equivalent native mechanism that would make this a faithful materialization rather than a translation shim.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report -- 2026-07-07
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-07-07
**APM Version**: 0.24.0 (b915f8d)
**Commands Inspected**: 29 (apm, init, install, uninstall, update, compile, run, deps, deps list, deps tree, deps info, deps clean, deps update, deps why, mcp, mcp list, mcp search, mcp show, mcp install, config, config set, config get, config list, config unset, runtime, runtime setup, runtime list, runtime status, runtime remove)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 1 |
| Medium | 2 |
| Low | 4 |

---

### High Severity

#### `intellij` listed in docs as a valid `--target` value but rejected by the CLI

- **Command**: `apm install --target intellij`
- **Problem**: The `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md` documentation explicitly lists `intellij` as a valid `--target` value, but the CLI rejects it at runtime with "Unknown target 'intellij'". The `intellij` identifier exists only as a runtime alias in `RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET` (mapping to `copilot`) and is not a first-class entry in `KNOWN_TARGETS`. Users who follow the docs and pass `--target intellij` will get an error.
- **Evidence**:
  - Docs (`install.md`, line 49): `Values: copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, intellij, vscode, agent-skills, all`
  - CLI output: `Error: [x] Unknown target 'intellij'` / `Valid targets: antigravity, claude, codex, copilot, cursor, gemini, kiro, opencode, windsurf`
  - Source: `RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET = {"vscode": "copilot", "agents": "copilot", "intellij": "copilot"}` in `src/apm_cli/integration/targets.py` -- `intellij` is a runtime alias only, not in `KNOWN_TARGETS`
- **Suggested Fix**: Remove `intellij` from the `--target` values list in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md`. Optionally add a note that `intellij` is accepted via the legacy `--runtime` flag only (which routes it to the `copilot` target).

---

### Medium Severity

#### `vscode` deprecated alias undocumented in `apm install --help` target list

- **Command**: `apm install --help` / `apm install --target vscode`
- **Problem**: `vscode` is a deprecated alias for `copilot` (present in `RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET`) and is silently accepted by `--target` in both `install` and `compile`. However, it is not mentioned at all in `apm install --help`'s `--target` description, creating a discoverability gap. The compile docs correctly document it as a deprecated alias, but the install docs list it alongside first-class targets without any deprecation note.
- **Evidence**:
  - `apm install --help` `--target` values: `copilot, claude, cursor, opencode, codex, gemini, antigravity, windsurf, kiro, agent-skills, all` (no `vscode`)
  - `apm install --target vscode --dry-run` succeeds silently (exit 0)
  - `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/compile.md`: "`vscode` and `agents` are accepted as deprecated aliases for `copilot` and emit a one-line warning."
  - `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/install.md` line 49 lists `vscode` without deprecation notice
- **Suggested Fix**: In `install.md`, add a deprecation note for `vscode` (and `agents`) consistent with how compile.md treats them. Optionally add a note to `apm install --help` that `vscode` is accepted as a deprecated alias.

#### `--runtime` help text lists `intellij` without listing `vscode`

- **Command**: `apm install --help` (`--runtime TEXT` option)
- **Problem**: The `--runtime` flag description lists "Target specific runtime only (copilot, claude, codex, cursor, gemini, antigravity, **intellij**, kiro, opencode, windsurf)" but omits `vscode`, which is also a valid runtime alias (maps to `copilot`). This creates asymmetry: `intellij` is listed but `vscode` is not, even though both are aliases in `RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET`.
- **Evidence**:
  - CLI help: `--runtime TEXT  Target specific runtime only (copilot, claude, codex, cursor, gemini, antigravity, intellij, kiro, opencode, windsurf)`
  - Source (`src/apm_cli/commands/install.py`, line 894): this string is hardcoded
  - `RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET` in `targets.py`: both `vscode` and `intellij` are aliases for `copilot`, but only `intellij` appears in the `--runtime` help
- **Suggested Fix**: Update the `--runtime` help string in `src/apm_cli/commands/install.py` to either include `vscode` (for symmetry) or add a note that these are deprecated runtime aliases. Align with the actual `RUNTIME_TO_CANONICAL_TARGET` dictionary.

---

### Low Severity

#### `--verbose` descriptions are stylistically inconsistent across commands

- **Commands**: All commands with `--verbose`
- **Problem**: The `--verbose` / `-v` flag has different descriptions across commands with no clear pattern:
  - `apm` (top-level): "Enable debug-level logging (equivalent to APM_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG)"
  - `apm init`: "Show detailed output"
  - `apm install`: "Show detailed installation information"
  - `apm uninstall`: "Show detailed removal information"
  - `apm update`: "Show unchanged deps and detailed pipeline diagnostics"
  - `apm compile`: "Show detailed source attribution and optimizer analysis"
  - `apm run`: "Show detailed output"
  - `apm mcp search`/`show`: "Show detailed output"
  - `apm deps update`: "Show detailed update information"
  - `apm deps list`: No `--verbose` flag at all
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize to either a short generic form ("Show detailed output") or a command-specific form consistently. Add `--verbose` to `apm deps list` if verbose output is meaningful there.

#### `-h` is not accepted as a shorthand for `--help`

- **Commands**: All commands
- **Problem**: `apm -h` (and `apm <subcommand> -h`) returns "Error: No such option: -h" with exit code 2. Many CLI tools and user conventions treat `-h` as equivalent to `--help`. Users accustomed to this pattern will encounter an error rather than help.
- **Evidence**: `$ apm -h` -> `Error: No such option: -h` (exit code 2)
- **Suggested Fix**: Configure `rich-click` / `click` to add `-h` as a short alias for `--help` at the top-level group and for each subcommand, or document in the CLI reference that only `--help` is supported (not `-h`).

#### `apm mcp install --help` does not surface forwarded options as proper CLI options

- **Command**: `apm mcp install --help`
- **Problem**: `apm mcp install` is an alias for `apm install --mcp`, and its `--help` output lists forwarded options as plain text (not as proper `Options:` entries). This means auto-completion, help parsers, and shell completions cannot discover those options from this subcommand. Users must read the explanation text and cross-reference `apm install --help`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Forwarded install options (see 'apm install --help' for the full list):
    --transport [stdio|http|sse|streamable-http]
    --url URL           Server URL for remote transports
    --env KEY=VALUE     Environment variable (repeatable)
    ...
    --dev / --dry-run / --force / --verbose / --no-policy
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Either expose the forwarded options as real Click options (with `is_eager=False` pass-through), or add a usage note in the CLI reference that directs users to `apm install --help` for the full option list. The current plain-text list is better than nothing but could mislead users into thinking only those options are available.

#### `--yes`/`-y` flag descriptions use inconsistent phrasing

- **Commands**: `apm init`, `apm update`, `apm deps clean`, `apm runtime remove`
- **Problem**: All use "Skip" or "Confirm" language but the phrasing differs:
  - `apm init`: "Skip interactive prompts and use auto-detected defaults"
  - `apm update`: "Skip the confirmation prompt (for CI / automation)"
  - `apm deps clean`: "Skip confirmation prompt"
  - `apm runtime remove`: "Confirm the action without prompting"
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize to a consistent template such as "Skip the confirmation prompt" across all commands.

---

### Clean Areas

The following commands and areas passed all checks with no issues found:

- `apm deps list`, `apm deps tree`, `apm deps info`, `apm deps clean`, `apm deps why`: correct help text, proper error messages for missing required arguments
